title: From a Galloping Horse to a Moving Train: How Cinema Was Born
title_zh: 从奔马到进站列车：电影是如何诞生的
intro_zh: 本文约535词，难度符合CET-4，建议阅读时间5-6分钟。

paragraphs.en: Cinema did not appear in a single bright moment. It grew from many small steps: a bet about a running horse, a roll of film, and a machine that could throw pictures onto a wall. In the late 1800s, inventors in Europe and America raced to turn still images into movement. Their work changed entertainment forever.
paragraphs.zh: 电影并非在某个明亮的瞬间突然出现。它由许多小步骤发展而来：一场关于奔马的打赌、一卷胶片，以及一台能把画面投到墙上的机器。19世纪末，欧洲和美国的发明家竞相把静止图像变成运动。他们的工作永远改变了娱乐。

paragraphs.en: Why does a fast series of pictures look like movement? The answer lies partly in the human eye and brain. When images appear quickly, about 16 to 24 per second, the mind fills the gaps. This is an illusion that makes a film feel alive. Early makers did not fully understand the science, but they used the effect well. This trick is called persistence of vision, and it still shapes every video we watch.
paragraphs.zh: 为什么快速连续的画面看起来像运动？答案部分在于人眼和大脑。当图像快速出现——大约每秒16到24幅——大脑会填补间隙。这是一种错觉，让电影显得有生命。早期制作者并未完全理解其中的科学，但他们很好地利用了这一效果。这种把戏被称为视觉暂留，它至今仍塑造着我们观看的每一段视频。

paragraphs.en: In 1878, the photographer Eadweard Muybridge set up a famous experiment in California. He placed 24 cameras along a track and used trip wires to capture a horse at full speed. The photos proved that all four feet leave the ground at once. The pictures were not a movie yet, but they showed how motion could be studied. His work also inspired inventors to build machines that could show many images in order.
paragraphs.zh: 1878年，摄影师埃德沃德·迈布里奇在加利福尼亚做了一个著名实验。他把24台相机沿跑道排开，并用绊线捕捉全速奔跑的马。照片证明四蹄会同时离地。这些照片还不是电影，但它们显示了运动如何被研究。他的工作也启发发明家制造能按顺序展示许多图像的机器。

paragraphs.en: The next step was to put such images on a strip of film. In the early 1890s, Thomas Edison's team built the Kinetoscope, a box that let one person watch a short film through a small hole. It was a clever machine, but it could not project pictures for a room full of people. That limit would soon be broken. Viewers paid a coin, put their eyes to the hole, and saw a short loop of action.
paragraphs.zh: 下一步是把这样的图像放到一条胶片上。19世纪90年代初，托马斯·爱迪生的团队造出了活动电影放映机，这是一个让一个人通过小孔观看短片的盒子。它是台聪明的机器，却不能为满屋子的人投射画面。这个限制很快就被打破了。观众付一枚硬币，把眼睛凑到孔前，看到一小段循环的动作。

paragraphs.en: On December 28, 1895, the Lumière brothers held a public show in Paris. Their Cinématographe was small, light, and able to project images onto a screen. An audience paid to see short scenes, including a train arriving at a station. Some viewers reportedly jumped back, afraid the train would run into them. The room was dark, the screen was white, and for the first time a crowd laughed and gasped together. Cinema had become a shared experience.
paragraphs.zh: 1895年12月28日，卢米埃尔兄弟在巴黎举行了一场公开放映。他们的电影机小巧、轻便，能把图像投射到屏幕上。观众花钱观看短场景，包括一列火车进站。据说有些观众吓得往后跳，害怕火车会撞到他们。黑暗的房间里，屏幕是白的，一群人第一次一起大笑和惊呼。电影成了一种共享体验。

paragraphs.en: At first, most films simply showed real life: a garden, a wave, a street. They were wonders of technology, not yet stories. The French magician Georges Méliès helped change that. He found that stopping the camera and starting it again could create surprising tricks. His 1902 film A Trip to the Moon used such effects to tell a playful narrative. The film was only about 14 minutes long, yet it opened the door to fantasy.
paragraphs.zh: 起初，大多数电影只是展示现实生活：花园、海浪、街道。它们是技术奇观，还不是故事。法国魔术师乔治·梅里爱帮助改变了这一点。他发现停下摄影机再重新开始可以创造惊人的戏法。他1902年的电影《月球旅行记》用这样的效果讲述了一个好玩的叙事。这部片只有约14分钟长，却打开了幻想之门。

paragraphs.en: As films grew longer, directors learned to edit shots into clear scenes. The Great Train Robbery (1903), about eleven minutes long, used several locations and a close-up of a gun. These choices helped viewers follow a story with action and tension. In 1927, The Jazz Singer added recorded voices, and silent cinema began to lose its place.
paragraphs.zh: 随着电影变长，导演学会把镜头剪辑成清晰的场景。《火车大劫案》（1903）约11分钟长，使用了多个地点和一个枪的特写。这些选择帮助观众跟随一个有动作和紧张感的故事。1927年，《爵士歌手》加入了录制的声音，无声电影开始失去地位。

paragraphs.en: So how was cinema born? It was not the work of one hero. It came from scientific curiosity, new machines, and artists who saw that moving pictures could do more than record the world. In only a few decades, a lab trick became a popular art form that still fills theaters today.
paragraphs.zh: 那么电影是如何诞生的？它不是一位英雄的作品。它来自科学好奇心、新机器，以及看到活动画面不仅能记录世界还能做更多事情的艺术家。仅仅几十年间，一个实验室戏法变成了一种至今仍让影院满座的大众艺术形式。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: One person in Paris invented cinema alone.
Cinema grew from technology and storytelling over time.
The Lumière brothers copied Edison's machine.
Early films were longer than modern films.
questions.explain: 文章说明电影不是一人一时发明，而是由视觉原理、摄影技术、放映设备和叙事艺术逐步发展而来，因此选第二项。

questions.q: Why did Muybridge place 24 cameras along the track?
options: To make a film with sound.
To capture a horse running at full speed.
To test a new kind of film color.
To teach actors how to ride.
questions.explain: 第三段明确提到他用24台相机和绊线捕捉全速奔跑的马，以研究运动，因此选第二项。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the Kinetoscope from paragraph 4?
options: It let a large crowd watch a film together.
It was invented by the Lumière brothers.
It allowed only one person to watch at a time.
It could record voices and music.
questions.explain: 第四段说活动电影放映机让一个人通过小孔看短片，不能为满屋子的人放映，因此可推断它一次只供一人观看。

questions.q: The word narrative in paragraph 6 is closest in meaning to ____.
questions.explain: 第六段说梅里爱用特效讲述一个好玩的narrative，结合上下文它指电影讲述的故事或叙事，因此选第二项。
